statement: The function returns successfully with value r. For every j with 0 <= j < len(r), r[j] is a vector of exactly two I64 values; write r[j] = [a_j, b_j]. The list of these pairs, in the order j = 0, 1, ..., len(r)-1, is exactly the list of all pairs (a,b) of integers with 0 <= a <= b < len(s) such that b - a + 1 >= 3, s[k] = s[a] for every k with a <= k <= b, (a = 0 or s[a-1] != s[a]), and (b + 1 = len(s) or s[b+1] != s[b]); this list is ordered by increasing first component a. Thus every returned pair is a maximal constant run of length at least 3, every such run is returned, and no other pair is returned.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: The function returns successfully: there exists a value r such that large_group_positions s evaluates to a successful result with value r. In particular it does not fail, panic, or overflow on the given constraints.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), len(r[j]) = 2. In other words, every produced interval is represented by exactly two I64 entries.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r) such that len(r[j]) = 2, writing a = r[j][0] and b = r[j][1], we have 0 <= a <= b < len(s).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for all j and k with 0 <= j < k < len(r), if len(r[j]) = 2 and len(r[k]) = 2, then r[j][0] < r[k][0]. Thus the represented intervals appear in strictly increasing order of start index.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r)-1, if len(r[j]) = 2 and len(r[j+1]) = 2, then r[j][1] < r[j+1][0]. Thus every two consecutive represented intervals are disjoint and ordered, with the end index of the earlier interval strictly less than the start index of the later interval.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r) such that len(r[j]) = 2, writing a = r[j][0] and b = r[j][1], for every k with a <= k <= b we have s[k] = s[a]. Thus a returned interval lies entirely inside one constant-character run.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r) such that len(r[j]) = 2, writing a = r[j][0] and b = r[j][1], we have b - a + 1 >= 3, s[k] = s[a] for every k with a <= k <= b, (a = 0 or s[a-1] != s[a]), and (b + 1 = len(s) or s[b+1] != s[b]). Thus every returned interval is a maximal constant run whose length is at least 3.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, for every a and b with 0 <= a <= b < len(s), if b - a + 1 >= 3, s[k] = s[a] for every k with a <= k <= b, (a = 0 or s[a-1] != s[a]), and (b + 1 = len(s) or s[b+1] != s[b]), then there exists j with 0 <= j < len(r) such that len(r[j]) = 2, r[j][0] = a, and r[j][1] = b. Thus every maximal constant run of length at least 3 is present in the output.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, len(r) equals the number of maximal constant runs of s whose length is at least 3, where a maximal constant run is a pair (a,b) with 0 <= a <= b < len(s), s[k] = s[a] for all k with a <= k <= b, (a = 0 or s[a-1] != s[a]), and (b + 1 = len(s) or s[b+1] != s[b]).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r, len(r) = 0 if and only if there is no index i with 0 <= i and i + 2 < len(s) and s[i] = s[i+1] = s[i+2]. Equivalently, the output is empty exactly when s contains no three equal consecutive bytes.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: The function returns successfully with value r. If len(s) >= 3 then len(r) = 1, len(r[0]) = 2, r[0][0] = 0, and r[0][1] = len(s) - 1. If len(s) < 3 then len(r) = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] = s[0].

statement: The function returns successfully with value r and len(r) = 0. In other words, when every adjacent pair of bytes differs, all constant runs have length 1 and no large group is returned.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s)-1, s[i] != s[i+1].

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r and len(r) > 0, writing a = r[0][0] (so r[0] is a two-element interval), a is the smallest integer i such that 0 <= i and i + 2 < len(s) and s[i] = s[i+1] = s[i+2]. That is, the first returned interval starts at the first position where three equal consecutive bytes begin.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns successfully with value r and len(r) > 0, writing b = r[len(r)-1][1] (so the last entry is a two-element interval), b is the largest integer i such that 2 <= i < len(s) and s[i-2] = s[i-1] = s[i]. That is, the last returned interval ends at the last position where three equal consecutive bytes end.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122.
